A_extra.issue: Dirty-limit coefficient in Eq. 2 is fixed by theory (hbar/(pi Delta0), about 1.38 pH K/Ohm); the fitted slope 16.3 is about 12x larger, so the dirty term explains only a few percent of Lk; also the pi dropped between SI Eq. 23 and 24
Mean free path inferred from SI Eq. 26 (about 0.6 nm) contradicts a 2D Drude estimate from the same Rs (kF l about 100, l of 10 to 20 nm)

Measured Lk is 3 to 27x above London plus dirty BCS terms; implied lambda (0.4 to 1.2 um, 750 nm from S5 intercept) inconsistent with the 230 nm used for the Pearl length; Pearl length from data is mm-scale
Fig. 4c slope rests almost entirely on the literature monolayer point (Rs, Tc from a different sample, Ref. 38); remaining points span small Rs/Tc range and scatter
Ratio below 1 for the 10-layer point makes xi0/l negative in Eq. 26, unphysical
Rs and Tc for 'this work' points come from separate DC flakes with sizeable flake-to-flake spread; measure R(T) on the microwave devices via the DC bias line

Aspect-ratio test to separate contact inductance from sheet inductance (fit Lk = L_contact + Lk,sq L/W), with a rough estimate of +/-25 pH; contact noise floor 0.01 Ohm inconsistent with Fig. S1c scatter
'1 layer = 1 nm' conversion wrong (2H-NbSe2 layer spacing about 0.63 nm); AFM and Raman thicknesses must be reconciled
Monolayer assignment of D1 is doubtful: monolayer has no shear mode, 19.04 cm^-1 implies N about 1.8, consistent with a bilayer
Raman shear mode saturates for N >= 6, so layer numbers there are not resolved
Lk,sq d is not constant; the dashed '1/d fit' in Fig. 4a cannot be pure A/d; state functional form, give log-log exponent, explain omission of D10 to D12
No uncertainties on Lk, Kerr coefficients, I*, d, Rs, Tc in Table 1
Participation-corrected loss: effective Q of NbSe2 element about 3e3 to 4e3, far below fluxonium needs; Qi rising with power suggests TLS loss
Superinductor magnitude: 38 Ohm/square reactance needs about 170 squares to reach R_Q
Kerr comparison across devices with different participation is not like-for-like; use j* or normalized K
Pearl-regime 'geometric confinement' mechanism is not stated; for W << Lambda thin-film electrodynamics gives no extra enhancement; W comparable to Lambda for D10 to D12
Kerr derivation (SI Eqs. 6 to 8): wrong quartic prefactor (1/2 vs 1/4 or 3/4), sign convention, recomputed K differs (5.7 vs 3.8 Hz); photon-number calibration uncertainty
Small bias range ((I/I*)^2 < 0.006) barely constrains I*; I* exceeds depairing current by a factor of a few in GL/Usadel
Temperature dependence Lk(T) and device Tc missing
Tiny Kerr coefficients of D10 to D12 must be shown to exceed control-resonator nonlinearity
Factor a in Eq. 25 is 0.75 in SI but 1 in main text

Internal numeric inconsistencies: 0.45 vs 0.55 GHz shift for D6, -90 vs -100 dBm onset, 30 vs 15 uA bias, Qi and fr values, Fig. 3c axis/sign, Table S3 arithmetic, attenuator stages, Fig. S7 caption, substrate
Spectator Qi = 5.985e6 poorly constrained when Qi/Qc about 60
n0 definition (Cooper pairs vs electrons) inconsistent with 2e, 2m
Broken inversion / Ising SOC statement should be layer-specific (bulk 2H is centrosymmetric)
Data availability statement too restrictive; deposit data

D10 to D12 absent from Fig. 4a and several devices absent from Fig. 4c without explanation
DC bias range: text says up to 30 uA, Fig. 3e,f axes stop at 15 uA; other measured ranges not disclosed
Data available only on request, no code
Power-dependent shift may be microwave pair breaking or quasiparticle heating rather than Kerr; measure fr, Qi versus bath temperature and use IQ-plane trajectories
Power and DC-bias sweeps shown only for D6; show a second device such as D1
Fit total Lk against squares/d with a constant offset term to bound contact/series inductance from Table 1
D10 to D12 Lk,sq two to three times above mu0 lambda^2/d with lambda about 230 nm
Table S3 row provenance (7-layer row missing from Table S1); sensitivity of Fig. 4c slope to the literature monolayer point and to D1 at 1.5 layers
Photon-number calibration in Eq. 5 (line attenuation, Qc) and its uncertainty
Rising Qi with power (Fig. S4c) versus reported linewidth broadening
